statement.definition_summary: Let G=Gal(C/R). The restriction of alpha in H_G^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)) to X(R), followed by the canonical map(1.57), has components alpha_p for p congruent to k modulo2. The topological subgroup0 is defined by alpha_{k+i}=Sq^i(alpha_k) for even i, with negative squares zero. For1-cycles on a D-dimensional variety, k=D-1 and Remark1.20(i) equivalently requires alpha_p=0 for p<k. Over real numbers, Hdg_G0 intersects this subgroup with the inverse image of ordinary Hodge(k,k) classes. RIHC means surjectivity of CH^k(X) to Hdg_G0. PartII keeps its stated scope R=real numbers or H^2(O_X)=0.

standard_prerequisites.statement: Stone-Weierstrass over the real numbers, Akbulut-King curve approximation and homology realization, multijet transversality, the Ischebeck-Schulting cycle representative theorem and Witt conic-section theorem are the stated author inputs. Full local author reductions and uses are retained.

core_obligations: Keep all six steps under one parent theorem, with the later support lemmas, not six independent IDs
Retain the approximation-to-algebraic-cycle argument and the trace/Leray/relative-vanishing-to-global-algebraicity core
Use the real numbers exactly; no extension to arbitrary real closed fields or import of extra hypotheses from Corollary6.5
proof_roadmap: Use algebraicity on the base and algebraic approximation of loops to subtract a cycle killing the real restriction.
Lift a base cycle with finite real support to kill push-forward while preserving the first reduction.
Pass to relative equivariant cohomology, then use the trace sequence and Leray spectral sequence on a suitable open base.
Use sign realization and relative vanishing to kill the remaining class off a subset of dimension at most one.
Filter the complement into curves and affine-line/conic bundles over curves, and recover global algebraicity by purity.
difficulty_reason: H3: the argument combines real algebraic approximation and deformation of loops with equivariant integral cycle classes, the singular-conic trace sheaf, relative Leray spectral sequences and a dimension-one-support algebraicity argument. Neither the formal push-forward nor the last localization step is the complete proof; the nonroutine local geometric and topological cores are supplied. The six proof steps are one theorem, not six independent questions.
